articles.title: Exploring the relationship between creativity and creative reasoning in the subject of Differential and Integral Calculus
articles.titleOriginal: Exploring the relationship between creativity and creative reasoning in the subject of Differential and Integral Calculus
articles.abstract: The study investigates the relationship between creativity and creative reasoning in the context of working with mathematical tasks in the subject of Differential and Integral Calculus. The research explores how these concepts manifest themselves and influence mathematical problem solving, with a qualitative approach and detailed analysis of a task. It highlights creativity as a developable ability and creative reasoning as a process of novelty, flexibility and plausibility. Strategies to stimulate its development in teaching are also discussed. The analysis suggests that encouraging creative reasoning in students, motivating them to explore different approaches and question constraints, promotes a deeper and more innovative understanding of mathematical concepts.

articles.title: From macro to micro: how do Brazilian educational normative documents guide creativity?
articles.titleOriginal: From macro to micro: how do Brazilian educational normative documents guide creativity?
articles.abstract: What are the normative guidelines for creativity in Basic Education? Based on an analysis of six Brazilian normative educational documents (LDB, DCN, BNCC, BNCC Computing, BNC-Formação and BNC-Formação Continuada), we sought to understand how creativity is addressed at the macro (institutional) and micro (pedagogical practices) levels. Methodologically, the investigation began by reading the titles of chapters and sections of the documents, followed by searching for keywords, such as create and creativity, and then analyzing the corresponding excerpts. The results show that although creativity is mentioned, its presence in teaching practice is limited. It is concluded that a continuous and strategic effort is needed to expand and make its inclusion more effective through both public policies and pedagogical practices.

articles.titleOriginal: Mathematical Creativity Tests for Basic Education: analysis in the field of Arithmetic and their potentialities:
articles.abstract: Creativity is considered an important ability that contribute to the individual’s integral formation, is valued in the job market and induces scientific/technological progress. In the mathematical context, it is defined as the ability to generate multiple solutions to problems. The objective of the study was to reflect on the potential of creativity in Mathematics test items for structuring pedagogical work in Basic Education. For this, research that applied specific tests were analyzed, considering the structure of the items and its content, to order to verify its potential for developing mathematical creativity. By results, the potencial of the items analysed were discussed, above all, as instruments for pedagogical work organization for stimulating the critical and creative potential in Mathematics of students.

En el contexto matemático, se define como la capacidad de generar múltiples soluciones a los problemas. Este estudio buscó reflexionar sobre el potencial de los ítems de pruebas de creatividad en Matemáticas para el trabajo pedagógico en la Educación Básica. Así, se analizaron investigaciones que realizó aplicaciones de pruebas, considerando la estructura de los ítems y contenidos involucrados, para visualizar potenciales para el desarrollo de la creatividad matemática. Como resultado, se discutieron potencialidades de los ítems, especialmente, como instrumentos organizativos del trabajo pedagógico para estimular el potencial crítico y creativo en Matemáticas de estudiantes.

The objective of the study was to reflect on the potential of creativity in Mathematics test items for structuring pedagogical work in Basic Education. For this, research that applied specific tests were analyzed, considering the structure of the items and its content, to order to verify its potential for developing mathematical creativity. By results, the potencial of the items analysed were discussed, above all, as instruments for pedagogical work organization for stimulating the critical and creative potential in Mathematics of students.

articles.title: Creative Mathematics: video production with 5th year Elementary School Students
articles.titleOriginal: Creative Mathematics: video production with 5th year Elementary School Students
articles.abstract: The study investigated the production of digital videos for teaching quantities and measurements in the 5th grade of Elementary School. Using a qualitative approach and intervention research, the active participation of students in the creation of videos that related mathematical concepts to everyday life, such as measurements in supermarkets, was analyzed. The experience favored active learning, promoting engagement, creativity, and the development of abilities such as communication, teamwork, and critical thinking. The videos facilitated the understanding of the content and made learning more dynamic. Despite the challenges in organization and editing, students highlighted the importance of collaboration. It is concluded that audiovisual production, in a participatory approach, is an effective resource for making mathematics teaching more accessible and meaningful.

The results indicate that this approach contributed to the development of students' autonomy, reasoning, argumentation, and creativity during the educational practice, advancing the understanding of mathematical concepts, with problem solving established as a pathway and guidance for learning.

articles.title: Digital video production: an invitation to creativity in Mathematics classes
articles.titleOriginal: Digital video production: an invitation to creativity in Mathematics classes
articles.abstract: The promotion of creativity in Mathematics lessons fosters an environment conducive to the development of active participants in their knowledge construction process. The approach to mathematical content through video production offers significant potential for teaching and learning. The study, of a qualitative nature, sought to reflect on how video production can stimulate creativity in Mathematics classes. The investigation was conducted at a technical school in the city São Paulo with 29 students from the Integrated Technical High School program. The analysis reveals that the act of producing videos supported the construction of knowledge in Analytical Geometry and that this practice provides an opportunity for a creative approach to the communication of mathematical ideas.

articles.title: Stories and Problem Solving in Mathematics: a path to the development of children's creative thinking in Preschool
articles.titleOriginal: Stories and Problem Solving in Mathematics: a path to the development of children's creative thinking in Preschool
articles.abstract: The research analyzed the development of creative thinking and the understanding of mathematical notions through practices that explore solving mathematical problems related to a children's story. The study is part of a qualitative research of the action-research type; presents discussions on creativity and the use of children's stories and problem-solving for its development. It also describes and analyzes a practice carried out with children in Prescchool. The data collection instruments used were: the records of the teacher-researcher and the children, as well as images. The analyses indicated that activities of this type stimulate children to seek out different strategies and resolutions, characteristics of creative thinking, and allow them to internalize the mathematical notions explored.

articles.title: Decolonial ethnomathematics and the ethnographic education of Mathematics teachers
articles.titleOriginal: Decolonial ethnomathematics and the ethnographic education of Mathematics teachers
articles.abstract: The study is justified by offering guidelines that help teachers understand the cultural and social challenges and demands of students, integrating them into the teaching of Mathematics. To this end, a theoretical foundation was developed based on Ethnomathematics, teacher education, Decoloniality and decolonial Ethnomathematics, to develop concepts that lead to on-demand ethnography as a possibility of affective/methodological education of Mathematics teachers through decolonial Ethnomathematics. The study, of a theoretical nature, is configured as an essay. In the end, three aspects for the affective/methodological education of teachers were identified: i) allowing oneself to be affected through a sentipensante attitude; ii) knowing the environment inserted by the precepts of on-demand ethnography and liberating pedagogy; iii) decoding of signs based on emic ethnomodeling.

articles.title: Between noesis and semiosis: Analytic Geometry in textbooks through the lens of Semiotic Representations
articles.titleOriginal: Between noesis and semiosis: Analytic Geometry in textbooks through the lens of Semiotic Representations
articles.abstract: This paper investigates how analytical geometry is addressed in two collections of textbooks approved by the 2021 National Textbooks and Didatic Materials Program. The research is qualitative in nature and supported by the Teorema System. The analysis, based on the Theory of Registers of Semiotic Representation, shows a predominance of treatment and conversion activities, especially calculation and translation between registers. There is a scarce presence of training activities, which suggests a more instructive than exploratory approach. It is concluded that, although the materials mobilize multiple registers, there are limitations in the connections between them, which may restrict the development of broader semiotic skills by students.

articles.title: The role of mathematical experimentation in the development of creativity
articles.titleOriginal: The role of mathematical experimentation in the development of creativity
articles.abstract: Mathematics in Brazil is still predominantly taught from the perspective of transmission of knowledge, and differentiated practices are largely scarce in the classroom. In contrast to this concept, experimentation presents itself as an innovative methodology which puts students in the center of the learning process, allowing them to create hypotheses, devise their own strategies, and develop their argumentation and creativity. Manipulatives support this process, enabling the exploration of diverse strategies and innovative solutions. From this perspective, the study sought to understand how the basic curriculum of Brazil (BNCC) and international guidance documents treat the relation between experimental activities and the development of creativity in students. To this end, a qualitative approach was adopted using documentary research to analyze the selected primary sources. The results indicate that mathematical creativity is promoted when pedagogical practices value reasoning, reflection and experimentation.

Los resultados indican que cuando las prácticas pedagógicas valorizan el raciocinio, la reflexión y la experimentación, se promueve la creatividad matemática.

articles.title: Investigating the concept of area for teaching and Creativity in Mathematics: interactions based on a story
articles.titleOriginal: Investigating the concept of area for teaching and Creativity in Mathematics: interactions based on a story
articles.abstract: This paper describes a virtual teacher education forum based on the perspective of Mathematics for Teaching and Problematized Mathematics. The data produced and presented derives from the story Imagined experience: the concept of area straight from the classroom and included multiple resolutions, ways of listening and shifts in the meanings of error and non-understanding. In methodological terms, considering the Development Research, there were indications of the potential and weaknesses of the Training Situation portrayed. In conclusion, the alignment with Creativity in Mathematics was found to be relevant, since it contributed to the mobilization of interactions, favoring the reorganization of Mathematics for teaching the concept of area to participants.

The pedagogical practice from the UDL perspective stimulated creativity and expanded access to knowledge, connecting Mathematics to everyday life.

articles.title: Dos padrões à generalização: como a criatividade é expressa por futuros professores do Brasil e de Portugal?
articles.titleOriginal: Dos padrões à generalização: como a criatividade é expressa por futuros professores do Brasil e de Portugal?
articles.titleEn: From patterns to generalization: how is creativity expressed by future teachers in Brazil and Portugal?
articles.abstract: O estudo investigou como futuros professores, brasileiros e portugueses, em formação inicial, resolviam problemas de generalização de padrões matemáticos, com ênfase nas múltiplas resoluções e na criatividade. A pesquisa adotou um paradigma qualitativo, exploratório, com foco na caracterização do desempenho dos participantes na resolução de tarefas envolvendo padrões figurativos, assim como nas dimensões da criatividade que emergiram nessas resoluções e nas variações entre os dois contextos. O estudo destaca a importância de integrar a visualização e a exploração de múltiplas representações na formação de futuros professores. Foi possível identificar que o foco na visualização em Portugal promove uma compreensão mais robusta das regularidades e generalizações algébricas e, no Brasil, o uso da notação simbólica favorece o desenvolvimento de habilidades formais.

The research adopted a qualitative and exploratory paradigm, focusing on characterizing the participants' performance in solving tasks involving figurative patterns, as well as the dimensions of creativity that emerged in these resolutions and the variations between the two contexts. The study highlights the importance of integrating visualization and the exploration of multiple representations in the training of future teachers. It is possible to identify that the focus on visualization in Portugal promotes a more robust understanding of algebraic regularities and generalizations, and in Brazil, the use of symbolic notation favors the development of formal skills.

articles.title: Neurodidactic analysis of the difficulty in learning the notion of rational number in the 3rd grade of Elementary School
articles.titleOriginal: Neurodidactic analysis of the difficulty in learning the notion of rational number in the 3rd grade of Elementary School
articles.abstract: The objective of this article was to analyze the monitoring and remediation of learning difficulties related to the ability to operate with the notion of rational numbers in the 3rd grade of Elementary School. The methodology used was documentary and bibliographical research, based on the Common National Curricular Base, followed by references from Cognitive Neuroscience and Mathematics Didactics to justify the neurodidactic analysis. In the practical explanations and pedagogical considerations to the teacher of the documents analyzed, weaknesses were found that could be mitigated by neurocognitive principles related to attentional functioning added to principles of the Theories of Didactic Situations and Didactic Engineering.

articles.title: The (In)visibility of motherhood in São Paulo curriculum documents: an analysis using the IRaMuTeQ software
articles.titleOriginal: The (In)visibility of motherhood in São Paulo curriculum documents: an analysis using the IRaMuTeQ software
articles.abstract: The research in this paper aims to investigate the representation of motherhood in curriculum documents, focusing on science and math classes. Methodologically, the IRaMuTeQ software enabled a detailed analysis of language patterns for the lexical and grammatical analysis of curriculum texts for Early Childhood Education, Elementary, Middle and High School, identifying recurring terms and their association with biological and reproductive concepts. The results show a predominance of a reductionist view of motherhood, confined to the biological field, in which the female body is addressed almost exclusively in reproductive terms. In relation to Mathematics, the absence of direct references to motherhood or parental care is notable, suggesting an invisibility of these themes in areas traditionally considered gender-neutral.

articles.titleOriginal: Etnografia no processo de des(construção) por uma Educação Matemática (Outra)
articles.titleEn: Ethnography in the process of des(construction) for a Mathematics Education (Other)
articles.abstract: A discussão apresentada neste ensaio objetiva promover autorreflexões que estabelecem conexões para uma Antropologia da Educação Matemática por meio da abordagem etnográfica. Trata-se de uma pesquisa autoetnográfica, desenvolvida em uma escrita criativa inspirada na conversação proposta por Alejandro Haber. Nesse diálogo, não se trata de transpor conceitos de uma área para outra, mas de externar como esses conceitos ressignificam perspectivas, as inquietações que provocam e os impactos no modo de fazer pesquisa. Os resultados evidenciam a importância de abordagens antropológicas na formação de educadores da Educação Matemática, em busca de uma Educação Matemática (Outra) que acolha vozes (Outras) e respeite a diversidade e culturas dos sujeitos nas pesquisas, abrindo caminho para novas formas de pesquisa nesse campo.

articles.title: A pesquisa em Educação Matemática: possibilidades de feitura e apreciação dos dados sob a perspectiva dos estudos antropológicos
articles.titleOriginal: A pesquisa em Educação Matemática: possibilidades de feitura e apreciação dos dados sob a perspectiva dos estudos antropológicos
articles.titleEn: Research in Mathematics Education: possibilities for making and appreciating data from the perspective of anthropological studies
articles.abstract: A reflexão apresentada neste ensaio teórico propõe repensar metodologias de pesquisa em Educação Matemática sob uma perspectiva antropológica, promovendo a feitura e apreciação dos dados em oposição à tradicional coleta e análise, propondo uma Educação Matemática mais sensível à diversidade cultural e contribuindo para uma epistemologia plural e contextualizada. Inspirado por uma visão crítica e decolonial, enfatiza-se a importância de métodos como a observação participante, narrativas e etnografias que permitem captar a complexidade cultural e social. Esse movimento visa contribuir para uma Educação Matemática enraizada na diversidade, valorizando a pluralidade de saberes culturais e incentivando o diálogo entre conhecimentos escolares e práticas locais. Assim, promove-se uma educação mais democrática, transformadora e conectada às realidades sociais dos estudantes.

Inspired by a critical and decolonial vision, it emphasizes the importance of methods such as participant observation, narratives and ethnographies that make it possible to capture cultural and social complexity. Assim, promove-se uma educação mais democrática, transformadora e conectada às realidades sociais dos estudantes.

articles.title: Os povos indígenas do Alto Rio Negro e a dominação econômica colonial nos anos 1970
articles.titleOriginal: Os povos indígenas do Alto Rio Negro e a dominação econômica colonial nos anos 1970
articles.titleEn: The indigenous peoples of the upper Rio Negro and colonial economic domination in the 1970’s
articles.abstract: O texto deste ensaio tem como objetivo analisar, sob uma perspectiva antropológica, o contexto colonial dos anos 70 no Alto Rio Negro, Amazonas, focando no contato entre os povos indígenas e os missionários, com base nas relações econômicas mediadas pelo sistema de troca. A questão central investigada foi: como eram realizadas as relações econômicas e as práticas matemáticas entre indígenas e missionários? A metodologia adotada se fundamenta em uma discussão analítica e em uma abordagem interdisciplinar da antropologia e matemáticas presentes no recém-lançado livro (Castro et al., 2024). Como resultado, destaca-se o registro da relação exploratória colonizadora interétnica, atravessada pelos saberes matemáticos e antropológicos.

The methodology adopted is based on an analytical discussion and interdisciplinary approach to anthropology and mathematics present in the recently released book (Castro et al., 2024) As a result, we highlight the record of the interethnic exploratory colonizing relationship permeated by mathematical and anthropological knowledge.

articles.title: Etnomatemática e Etnografia, uma possibilidade antropológica
articles.titleOriginal: Etnomatemática e Etnografia, uma possibilidade antropológica
articles.titleEn: Ethnomathematics and Ethnography, an anthropological possibility
articles.abstract: A discussão abordada neste ensaio destaca a abordagem etnográfica e sua relevância na pesquisa etnomatemática, ressaltando sua importância para a compreensão do conhecimento matemático tradicional. Os conceitos de tornar-se feiticeiro, tornar-se mandira e tornar-se criança, ilustram a transformação dinâmica do pesquisador no contato com realidades culturais permeadas por crenças e mitos. Essas noções evidenciam que a relação entre pesquisadores e comunidades não se limita à observação, mas demanda uma imersão profunda que possibilita a coconstrução de conhecimento e uma compreensão ampliada das identidades culturais. Essas perspectivas também contribuem para uma Educação Matemática mais inclusiva, valorizando a diversidade de saberes e experiências.

articles.abstractEn: The discussion in this essay highlights the ethnographic approach and its relevance in ethnomathematical research, emphasizing its importance for understanding traditional mathematical knowledge. The concepts of becoming a sorcerer, becoming a mandira and becoming a child, illustrate the dynamic transformation of the researcher in contact with cultural realities permeated by beliefs and myths. These notions show that the relationship between researchers and communities is not limited to observation, but requires a deep immersion that enables the co-construction of knowledge and a broader understanding of cultural identities. These perspectives also contribute to a more inclusive Mathematics Education, valuing the diversity of knowledge and experiences.

articles.title: Eles observam uma imagem e nós, pela antropologia visual, observamos uma Geometria no esqueleto da casa de pau a pique
articles.titleOriginal: Eles observam uma imagem e nós, pela antropologia visual, observamos uma Geometria no esqueleto da casa de pau a pique
articles.titleEn: They observe an image and we, through visual anthropology, observe a Geometry in the skeleton of the wattle and daub house
articles.abstract: A ida ao campo, de modo que essa imersão permita o contato com o outro, caracteriza a produção de dados no fazer antropológico clássico. Em uma Antropologia em que os nativos se expressem por meio de imagens, abre-se a possibilidade de usá-la como campo e instrumento de pesquisa, em vez de serem apenas registros de observação. Na discussão presente neste ensaio, procurou-se identificar, a partir da imersão por observação, em uma perspectiva antropológica visual, os conceitos geométricos presentes no esqueleto de uma casa de pau a pique e suas articulações com o ensino. Os resultados evidenciaram que o esqueleto é sustentado por retângulos, quadrados, trapézios e triângulos, resultantes das interseções entre paus e/ou madeiras horizontais, verticais e oblíquos.

articles.abstractEn: Going to the field, so that this immersion allows contact with others, characterizes the production of data in classical anthropological practice. In an Anthropology in which natives express themselves through images, the possibility of using it as a field and research instrument opens up, instead of just being observation records. In the discussion present in this essay, we sought to identify, based on observational immersion, in a visual anthropological perspective, the geometric concepts present in the skeleton of a wattle and daub house and their connections with teaching. The results showed that the skeleton is supported by rectangles, squares, trapezoids and triangles, resulting from the intersections between horizontal, vertical and oblique sticks and/or wood.

articles.title: Confluências possíveis entre Antropologia e a perspectiva indisciplinar-decolonial
articles.titleOriginal: Confluências possíveis entre Antropologia e a perspectiva indisciplinar-decolonial
articles.titleEn: Possible confluences between Anthropology and the indisciplinary-decolonial perspective
articles.abstract: Neste ensaio autoetnográfico, apresenta-se uma descrição comentada sobre a prática de pegar neném das parteiras e a confluência entre as práticas socioculturais e a Antropologia da Educação Matemática, ressignificando a formação de docentes na Amazônia Paraense, sob uma perspectiva indisciplinar e decolonial. A pesquisa se propõe a desconstruir a colonialidade do conhecimento, inserindo-o nos debates atuais sobre a formação de docentes, entendendo a complexidade desse campo. Utilizando uma abordagem autoetnográfica, são compartilhadas experiências pessoais, acadêmicas e comunitárias relacionadas à formação docente, refletindo criticamente sobre o impacto de práticas socioculturais marginalizadas e como essas podem ser incorporadas no ensino como ferramentas de resistência para desafiar os modos de fazer pesquisas acadêmicas.

articles.abstractEn: This autoethnographic essay presents an annotated description of the Midwives' practice of picking up a baby and the confluence between socio-cultural practices and the Anthropology of Mathematics Education, giving new meaning to teacher training in the Para Amazon, from an indisciplinary and decolonial perspective. The research aims to deconstruct the coloniality of knowledge, inserting it into current debates on teacher training, understanding the complexity of this field. Using an autoethnographic approach, personal, academic and community experiences related to teacher training are shared, critically reflecting on the impact of marginalized socio-cultural practices and how these can be incorporated into teaching as tools of resistance to challenge the ways of doing academic research.

articles.title: Teoria Ator-Rede para pesquisa antropológica em Educação Matemática
articles.titleOriginal: Teoria Ator-Rede para pesquisa antropológica em Educação Matemática
articles.titleEn: Actor-Network Theory for anthropological research in Mathematical Education
authors: Oliveira, Luiz Antonio Ribeiro Neto de
articles.abstract: Este artigo apresenta um ensaio teórico acerca da instauração de etnografias problematizadoras para estudos em Educação Matemática. Para essa instauração, adotaram-se as perspectivas da Teoria Ator-Rede e das Práticas Matemáticas Indisciplinares, estruturadas nas seguintes etapas: buscar uma porta de entrada, identificar os porta-vozes, acessar os dispositivos de inscrição, identificar a prática matemática, analisar seus efeitos e afetos e mapear as ligações da rede. A coleta de dados foi realizada por meio do fotovoz, e a Cartografia de Controvérsias foi aplicada na exploração de petróleo na foz do rio Amazonas. Espera-se que essa proposta seja modelo para atividades a serem debatidas em sala de aula, fomentando uma Matemática ética, estética e voltada para a promoção da cidadania.

articles.titleOriginal: Calculus I: reflections constructed within the scope of the UESB Interdisciplinary Institutional Tutorial Education Program
articles.abstract: This qualitative study aimed to foster reflection on the teaching of Calculus I in undergraduate courses offered by a department at the Southwest Bahia State University, Brazil. The aim was to deepen and solidify the training of students in the university's Interdisciplinary Institutional Tutorial Education Program. Data were collected through analysis of institutional documents, a questionnaire, and semi-structured interviews. The reflections enabled students to identify mathematical objects in which undergraduate students have difficulty understanding how these may interfere with the learning of Calculus I, as well as to propose solutions to minimize these difficulties. The study concluded that it effectively contributed to the training of students in the Program, particularly regarding research and the resulting discoveries.

articles.title: Exploring connections between Financial Education and the World of Work: an approach to wage taxation
articles.titleOriginal: Exploring connections between Financial Education and the World of Work: an approach to wage taxation
articles.abstract: This paper is the result of a master's thesis and analyzes how Financial Education can help Integrated High School students understand the tax implications in their financial lives. Using a qualitative intervention research methodology, the proposal suggests two classes with activities based on Scenarios for Investigation. The proposal highlights the importance of understanding the tax nuances related to employment, going beyond the market perspective. The results reveal that students questioned the fairness of tax rates, showing the influence of Financial Education on reflection about the challenges of the World of Work and tax issues. The study highlights the importance of integrating Financial Education, taxation, and the World of Work in order to educate students to make informed decisions and contribute to a more just society.

articles.title: Cassava flour production in the Quilombola Santa Luzia do Maruanum Community: following ethnomathematical paths
articles.titleOriginal: Cassava flour production in the Quilombola Santa Luzia do Maruanum Community: following ethnomathematical paths
articles.abstract: The process of producing flour begins with the planting of cassava and ends with the roasting and sale of the products. Observing this process encourages us to look at the ethnomathematical paths of this production and apply them to the classroom. In this context, the objective is to analyze the production of cassava flour in the knowledge/doing for socioeconomic equity in the Quilombola Santa Luzia do Maruanum Community. The qualitative approach and ethnographic research allow the use of instruments such as discussion circles, participant observation, and audio and video capture. However, Mr. José do Carmo's narrative is the focus of the analyses, discussions, and results. It is concluded that the beings, knowledge, and doings make it possible to contextualize some school mathematical concepts, reinforcing identities and local belonging.

articles.title: Fruit production in the Matapi Agricultural Colony and Ethnomathematics: contributions and frontiers
articles.titleOriginal: Fruit production in the Matapi Agricultural Colony and Ethnomathematics: contributions and frontiers
articles.abstract: The research aimed to analyze fruit production as a sustainability strategy in knowledge/practice and survival in the Matapi Agricultural Colony. Using a qualitative approach and ethnographic research, techniques such as participant observation and group discussions were used. Reference is made to the studies of D’Ambrosio (2011, 2020), Mattos (2015), Mattos (2020), Mesquita (2023), among others. The narratives of Mrs. Raimundinha and her son are presented in the discussions and results, addressing the concept of Ethnomathematics in approaches with the dimensions formulated by D'Ambrosio (2011) and the affective dimension created by Mattos (2020). It is concluded that pineapple production enables dialogue and exchange between local beings, knowledge, and practices, as well as some school mathematical concepts.

articles.title: Deaf teacher, inclusive practices, and ethnomathematical perspectives in the regular classroom
articles.titleOriginal: Deaf teacher, inclusive practices, and ethnomathematical perspectives in the regular classroom
articles.abstract: This paper presents the results of a study that aimed to examine the presence of a deaf teacher in regular classes in the Elementary School. Using Ethnomathematics as a theoretical and methodological reference, data were generated from a study group comprising hearing and deaf teachers who worked with deaf students in two public schools in municipalities in Mato Grosso, Brazil. The participants designed, developed, evaluated, and redesigned tasks using GeoGebra as an assistive technology. The analysis showed that deaf teachers can work in regular classrooms, provided they have the support of a professional Brazilian Sign Language (Libras) translator-interpreter.

articles.title: The Tipiti of Colonialities: oppression and insurgencies in teaching practices in Amazonian riverside communities
articles.titleOriginal: The Tipiti of Colonialities: oppression and insurgencies in teaching practices in Amazonian riverside communities
articles.abstract: This paper reports part of the results of a doctoral thesis that investigated traces and effects of coloniality in the practices of teachers who teach Mathematics in riverside communities in the rural area of ​​Manaus. From conversations with participating teachers, the idea of Tipiti of Colonialities emerged, inspired by a technology used by indigenous peoples to squeeze wild cassava, remove its poison, and produce food. As a theoretical reference, we explore connections between Decolonial Thought and Ethnomathematics as a way to visualize paths of insurgency in teaching practices in Mathematics. The results indicate that, despite public school management practices distancing students from their territories, teachers find ways to subvert the Tipiti de Colonialidades, as indigenous peoples teach us.

articles.title: Calculation strategies of sugarcane workers regarding their work journeys
articles.titleOriginal: Calculation strategies of sugarcane workers regarding their work journeys
articles.abstract: This study analyzed the strategies used by a sugarcane worker to determine the remuneration of a sugarcane cutter, considering his roles as cutter, overseer, and inspector. The objective was to understand and explain his perceptions through cell phone-recorded interviews about his professional trajectory, which characterizes a qualitative case study. As a result, the adoption of unusual methods was observed, such as transforming triangles into rectangles and decomposing the area of ​​land with elevations, without resorting to procedures taught in school. The interaction between the overseer, the inspector, and the cutters in measuring the areas reveals conflicts related to benefits and losses, demonstrating an awareness of the need to avoid social injustices.

articles.title: Origin and decline of the scientific discipline Descriptive Geometry
articles.titleOriginal: Origin and decline of the scientific discipline Descriptive Geometry
authors: Almeida, Ana Mary Fonseca Barreto de
articles.abstract: Descriptive Geometry originated with the creation of the École Centrale des Travaux Publics, later renamed École Polytechnique. Two arts — Architecture and Fortification — were taken as teaching subjects, giving rise to this scientific discipline. The study aimed to analyze the process of rise, transformation, and decline of Descriptive Geometry, with a qualitative character, through the methodology of textual and contextual analysis. The École Polytechnique suffered a severe crisis between modernist and empiricist engineers, separating theoretical and practical teaching. Thus, the analyses reveal that the decline of this discipline occurred approximately fifteen years after its creation, with a complexity of social, cultural, epistemological, and corporatist factors and dimensions causing this decline.

Son dos las artes — Arquitectura y Fortificación — tomadas como objetos de enseñanza que darán origen a esta disciplina científica. articles.title: Graph of an affine function: a study from the perspective of the Potential Didactic Contract
articles.titleOriginal: Graph of an affine function: a study from the perspective of the Potential Didactic Contract
authors: Andrade, Vladimir Lira Veras Xavier de
articles.abstract: The research aimed to investigate the potential didactic contract through expectations, potential contract rules, and indications of rupture present in a 1st-grade High School Mathematics textbook regarding the knowledge of the graph of the affine function. The technique adopted was document analysis, taking as a reference the definition of the elements that compose this contract. A total of three expectations, one potential explicit rule, three potential implicit rules, and two indications of rupture were identified. The results point to regularities that show a tendency towards standardization of the procedures for constructing the graph of the affine function, revealing both the strength of these regularities and their possible limits for the production of broader mathematical meanings.

articles.title: Mathematical tasks on Probability in 6th-grade Middle School textbooks approved by the PNLD 2024
articles.titleOriginal: Mathematical tasks on Probability in 6th-grade Middle School textbooks approved by the PNLD 2024
articles.abstract: Mathematical tasks (TM) are present in teaching materials and are widely used by teachers. They come in various types and serve different purposes during class. The study aimed to understand the role of TM proposed by textbooks (LD) for teaching Probability in the 6th grade of Middle School, as approved by the PNLD 2024. Using a qualitative approach, thirteen collections were examined, identifying the number of TM on Probability and analyzing the potential (or lack thereof) of some of them. The results reveal the predominance of TM with low cognitive demand, with a scarce presence of open proposals and an absence of investigative TM. The analysis highlights conceptual and methodological gaps that limit the development of students' probabilistic literacy. As a result, there is a need to reconfigure the tasks in the textbooks, with greater emphasis on contextualized and investigative proposals.

Las tareas matemáticas (TM) están presentes en los materiales didácticos y son ampliamente utilizadas por los docentes. Son de diversos tipos y tienen propósitos distintos durante la clase. El estudio tuvo como objetivo comprender el papel de las TM propuestas por libros de texto (LD) para la enseñanza de la Probabilidad en el 6º grado de la Enseñanza Fundamental, aprobados en el PNLD 2024. A través de un enfoque cualitativo, se examinaron trece colecciones, identificando la cantidad de TM relacionadas con la Probabilidad y analizando el potencial (o su ausencia) de algunos ejemplos seleccionados. El análisis evidencia lagunas conceptuales y metodológicas que limitan el desarrollo del alfabetismo probabilístico de los estudiantes. Como resultado, se identifica la necesidad de reconfigurar las tareas en los LD, con mayor énfasis en propuestas contextualizadas e investigativas.

articles.title: A reading on the development of the three editions of the Pedagogical Residency Program from the perspective of a professor educator
articles.titleOriginal: A reading on the development of the three editions of the Pedagogical Residency Program from the perspective of a professor educator
articles.abstract: The objective of the study was to analyze the three editions of the development of subprojects of the Pedagogical Residency Program (PRP) at the Federal University of Alfenas, focusing on the education aspect of students and the education professor who advisor the Licentiate Degree in Mathematics. To this end, an analysis of the professor educator's actions and notes was carried out, based on the assumptions of the Model of Semantic Fields, in particular plausible reading. Each edition of the PRP contributed to the education of the teacher education by enabling deep immersion in schools, bringing them closer to professional practice and also to the advisor who made changes to the subprojects in light of previous experiences, constantly (re)thinking the orientation process.

articles.title: Analysis of teaching learning mobilized by residents in the Pedagogical Residency Program in Mathematics
articles.titleOriginal: Analysis of teaching learning mobilized by residents in the Pedagogical Residency Program in Mathematics
articles.abstract: The objective of the research reported in this paper was to analyze the learning revealed by graduates of the Pedagogical Residency Program (PRP) in Minas Gerais, Brazil, as they reflected on their participation in Mathematics subprojects. To this end, the assumptions of Social Learning Theory were used. This is a qualitative study with 102 residents who responded to a semi-structured questionnaire. The data was organized into four categories, involving learning as belonging, as doing, as experience, and as transformation. The results indicate a sense of belonging, the development of projects and activities related to teaching practice, and the creation of education spaces. It is concluded that the PRP has established itself as a place for teacher education by promoting integration into the school context, dialogue, and the collective construction of knowledge.

articles.title: Creencias del profesor sobre material bibliográfico para enseñar Matemáticas en Educación Media Superior
articles.titleOriginal: Creencias del profesor sobre material bibliográfico para enseñar Matemáticas en Educación Media Superior
articles.titleEn: Teacher beliefs about bibliographic material to teach Mathematics in High School
articles.abstract: El objetivo del estudio fue identificar las creencias de dos profesoras acerca del material curricular bibliográfico para la enseñanza de las Matemáticas en Educación Media Superior. Para ello, se llevó a cabo un estudio descriptivo, con un enfoque cualitativo, configurado como un estudio de caso. Los dados fueron producidos mediante entrevista semiestructurada y posteriormente analizados a partir de dos categorías emergentes: criterios para la utilización del material bibliográfico y criterios para la selección de dicho material. Los resultados muestran que las creencias de ambos profesores están relacionadas con la percepción que tienen sobre cómo aprenden sus estudiantes, tomando como referencia las normativas de la institución en la que trabajan y las experiencias vividas por los profesores en su trayectoria como estudiantes.

The results show that the beliefs of both teachers are related to their perceptions of how their students learn, taking as reference the institutional regulations in which they work and the experiences lived by the teachers throughout their own trajectories as students.

articles.title: A look at non-Euclidean Geometries in Basic Education
articles.titleOriginal: A look at non-Euclidean Geometries in Basic Education
articles.abstract: The research presented in this article analyzed a teacher's reflective narrative on teaching non-Euclidean Geometries in Basic Education. Her experience is tied to her practice in schools, teacher education, and engagement with Mathematics Education. Qualitative analysis of the narrative showed that the inclusion of this content can broaden understanding of geometry, promote interdisciplinary connections, and contribute to citizenship education. However, challenges are highlighted, such as the scarcity of this content in textbooks, school curriculum, and Mathematics teacher’s education, as well as tensions between Euclidean and non-Euclidean concepts. It is concluded that working with this content in Basic Education can stimulate critical thinking, creativity, and the view of Mathematics as a human construct.

La investigación presentada en este artículo analizó la narrativa reflexiva de una profesora experimentada sobre la enseñanza de las Geometrías no Euclidianas en la Educación Básica. Su experiencia está relacionada con su actuación en la escuela, la formación de profesores de matemáticas y al compromiso con la Educación Matemática. El análisis cualitativo de su narrativa evidenció que la inserción de las Geometrías no Euclidianas puede ampliar la comprensión de las geometrías, promover conexiones interdisciplinarias y contribuir a la formación ciudadana. Sin embargo, se destacan desafíos como la escasez de contenidos sobre Geometrías no Euclidianas en libros didácticos, currículos escolares y en la formación de profesores de Matemáticas, además de tensiones entre conceptos euclidianos y no euclidianos. Se concluye que el trabajo con Geometrías no Euclidianas en la Educación Básica puede estimular el pensamiento crítico, la creatividad y la visión de las Matemáticas como construcción humana.

articles.abstract: This paper is part of a dissertation that developed Mathematical Modeling practices in the classroom and on a walking track, using the structure of a Mathematical Modeling Cycle as a theoretical reference. The research analyzed how the mobilization of mathematical content occurred, highlighting the potential of the approach. The methodology proved effective in expanding content development, achieving skills at subsequent levels, and improving essential skills for citizenship training.

articles.title: World hunger from the perspective of members of the Pedagogical Residency Program: contributions from Critical Mathematics Education
articles.titleOriginal: World hunger from the perspective of members of the Pedagogical Residency Program: contributions from Critical Mathematics Education
articles.abstract: The qualitative study whose objective is to identify, from the perspective of the advisor and the preceptor of a Pedagogical Residency Program, dialogues between a project developed with sixth-grade classes in a public school, focused on the theme of world hunger, and the principles of Critical Mathematics Education (CME). The stages of the project were analyzed in light of discussions in CME, which seeks to train students to develop a critical view of the society in which they live and to think about possibilities for transforming it. This process gave rise to some significant dialogues between the project and CME, especially those related to the exploration of Mathematics beyond calculation, the type of communication established in Mathematics classes, and the practices of reading and writing about the world mediated by Mathematics.

articles.title: Meanings and perceptions of undergraduate Mathematics students regarding written textual production as educational practice
articles.titleOriginal: Meanings and perceptions of undergraduate Mathematics students regarding written textual production as educational practice
articles.abstract: This study sought to understand the meanings and perceptions of undergraduate Mathematics students regarding written text production during their education, relating them to the development of teacher identity and Mathematics teaching. Based on frameworks that discuss writing as a discursive and educational practice, a qualitative approach was adopted, with intentional sampling of students in the 1st and 7th semesters and data collection via an online questionnaire. Enunciations were examined through content analysis, revealing subcategories such as incentives and opportunities, confidence in expressing mathematical concepts, and challenges in appropriating written language. The lack of systematic writing practices in the curriculum and the need to incorporate it as a structuring dimension of initial education were identified.

articles.title: Technological resources and their (possible) use in the initial education of Mathematics teachers
articles.titleOriginal: Technological resources and their (possible) use in the initial education of Mathematics teachers
authors: Almeida, Shirley Patrícia Nogueira de Castro e
articles.abstract: We analyzed excerpts from interviews with graduates of the Mathematics Degree Course at Unimontes, who graduated between 2020 and 2023, regarding their perceptions of the technological resources available on the course, and whether or not they were used by teachers and the reasons for this. Methodologically based on Oral History, we conducted interviews with 17 graduates of this program. We concluded that there are technological resources available, but not all teachers use them, even in subjects where technology could be an ally, such as Differential and Integral Calculus. Thus, it can be inferred that the challenge of integrating digital technologies into initial teacher education goes beyond the mere provision of physical infrastructure.

articles.title: Pedagogical Residency Program: reflections on its contributions to initial teacher education
articles.titleOriginal: Pedagogical Residency Program: reflections on its contributions to initial teacher education
articles.abstract: This study aimed to analyze the contribution of the Pedagogical Residency Program at Unimontes, Mathematics subproject, to the initial education of its graduates, investigating the extent to which the Program has fostered the development of the knowledge, skills, and competencies required for high-quality teaching in Basic Education. Methodologically, a questionnaire comprising open and closed-ended questions was administered to 44 residents in the subproject. The findings indicate that the Program played a significant role in initial teacher education by providing both theoretical and practical foundations for teaching practice, as well as by contributing to licentiate students' retention in the undergraduate program and strengthening their professional identity.

articles.title: Pedagogical Residency Program: education of educators
articles.titleOriginal: Pedagogical Residency Program: education of educators
articles.abstract: This research is descriptive in nature, qualitative in approach, and part of a project conceived and developed collaboratively by a network of researchers from Minas Gerais, Brazil, who are dedicated to researching the Pedagogical Residency Program. The research focused on the education of educators, considering both the advisor and the preceptor as co-trainers of the residents, seeking to understand the contributions of participation in the Program to the education of Mathematics educators teacher. Data from questionnaires answered by the preceptors were analyzed. These data enable reflection on the experiences of Higher Education Institutions in Minas Gerais and point to practices that have proven successful in the process of immersing future teachers in the school context.

articles.title: Potential of the Pedagogical Residency Program in the education of Mathematics teachers at the Federal University of Uberlândia
articles.titleOriginal: Potential of the Pedagogical Residency Program in the education of Mathematics teachers at the Federal University of Uberlândia
articles.abstract: This paper discusses the potential of the Pedagogical Residency Program (PRP) in the education of Mathematics teachers. The analysis, based on the assumptions of paradigmatic analysis, used reports from residents of the Mathematics course at the Federal University of Uberlândia (UFU), Santa Monica campus, linked to the Interdisciplinary Center for Physics and Mathematics, during eighteen months of the third PRP call for applications. The results indicate that, among other potentialities, the problematization of the theme of assessment proved to be important, leading to the recognition of its formative relevance. In this sense, the PRP contributed to the constitution of an unprecedented-viable: the possible creation of a curriculum component focused on the study of assessment in the Licentiate Degree in Mathematics at UFU.

articles.title: Didactic-Mathematical Knowledge in the initial education of Mathematics teachers: an analysis within the context of the Pedagogical Residency Program
articles.titleOriginal: Didactic-Mathematical Knowledge in the initial education of Mathematics teachers: an analysis within the context of the Pedagogical Residency Program
articles.abstract: This study analyzed the reflections of pre-service Mathematics teachers regarding the learning opportunities provided by the Pedagogical Residency Program, focusing on the development of the knowledge required for teaching. The theoretical framework is grounded in the Didactic-Mathematical Knowledge model. The study is qualitative in nature, adopting an interpretive approach, with data generated through questionnaires and semi-structured interviews and analyzed using Content Analysis. The analysis is organized into two categories corresponding to the ecological and interactional facets. The findings indicate that the practices developed by the pre-service teachers foster reflective processes about teaching and contribute to the development of professional knowledge. It is concluded that the Pedagogical Residency Program constitutes a formative space for the construction of teaching knowledge, even in challenging contexts.

articles.titleEn: Mathematics teaching practice: contextualized knowledge in decoloniality planetary-complexity
articles.abstract: El objetivo del ensayo fue analizar la práctica pedagógica de la Matemática: saberes contextualizados en la decolonialidad planetaria-complejidad. Para ello usamos las transmetodologías decoloniales planetaria complejas, con el transmétodo la hermenéutica comprensiva ecosófica y diatópica pasando por los momentos analíticos, empíricos y propositivos. En el momento analítico-empírico estudiamos consultando a autores originales de las categorías de estudio la práctica pedagógica de la Matemática en la tradicionalidad modernista-postmodernista. En los momentos propositivos nos desprendemos de la cita de autores y vamos a concretar el objetivo de estudio con la práctica pedagógica de la Matemática — saberes contextualizados en la decolonialidad planetaria-complejidad y las conclusiones no definitivas.

articles.title: Mathematics education for peace: from micro to macro
articles.titleOriginal: Mathematics education for peace: from micro to macro
articles.abstract: The research in this theoretical essay proposes an understanding of mathematics education for peace in the micro and macro dimensions, relating it to understandings of microviolence and macroviolence inside and outside the classroom. For this purpose, national literature was consulted. It is argued that this education requires continuous vigilance over the (re)production and (trans)formation of violence, with a view to rejecting it. These forms of violence are understood in the historical, social, and political contexts of a given era and understood as an open field. It also defends the existence of an open transition between micro and macro violence in mathematics education, experienced in a unique way by individuals.

Para ello, consultamos la literatura nacional. En resumen, entendemos que la educación matemática para la paz, en sus dimensiones micro y macro, está siempre atenta a las (re)producciones y (trans)formaciones de los conceptos de violencia, con el objetivo de rechazarlas. Además, argumentamos que la violencia es relativa al contexto histórico, social y político de una época determinada y puede entenderse como un campo abierto. Consideramos que entre la microviolencia y la macroviolencia en la educación matemática debe existir una zona de transición abierta, experimentada y percibida de forma única por cada individuo.

articles.title: Ethnomodelling research at GEPTEMaC: paths and reflections of a scientific collective
articles.titleOriginal: Ethnomodelling research at GEPTEMaC: paths and reflections of a scientific collective
articles.abstract: The research reported in this article presents the Study and Research Group on Trends in Mathematics Education and Culture (GEPTEMaC), highlighting its role in Mathematics Education through the analysis of ongoing and ongoing Ethnomodeling investigations. The theoretical and methodological paths taken, the collective reflections, and the contributions to the dialogue between culture and mathematics are highlighted. Qualitative and theoretical in nature, the investigation adopted the methodological procedure of analyzing 21 academic productions — at the undergraduate, master's, and doctoral levels — examined using the Content Analysis technique. The results point to Ethnomodeling as a possibility that values ​​culture in studies, recognizing mathematical knowledge and practices in sociocultural environments. GEPTEMaC has strengthened the academic debate and expanded its national reach.

articles.title: Making a box for honey production: conversations with a rural producer
articles.titleOriginal: Making a box for honey production: conversations with a rural producer
articles.abstract: The theme of this article is the construction of wooden boxes intended for honey production by bees. These boxes are located on the rural property of a small producer in Córrego Central, in the community of Cristalino, municipality of Nova Venécia, Espírito Santo. The objective of the research was to investigate the mathematization strategies of small farmers in the construction of beehives. It is found that the construction of beehives can be used as a didactic resource to assist in the teaching and learning of mathematical concepts of plane and spatial geometry. It is concluded that the mathematical practice of the rural producer acts as a subsidy for students to produce knowledge, through the articulation between concrete and abstract thinking, within the scope of geometric concepts.

articles.title: Ethnomathematics and Enawenê-Nawê Culture: the processes of generation, updating, and dissemination of knowledge in the rituals at Iyaõkwa Hakolone
articles.titleOriginal: Ethnomathematics and Enawenê-Nawê Culture: the processes of generation, updating, and dissemination of knowledge in the rituals at Iyaõkwa Hakolone
articles.abstract: This research analyzed the processes of construction of the Iyaõkwa Hakolone ritual house of the Enawenê-Nawê people from the perspective of Ethnomathematics, seeking to understand how mathematical knowledge emerges in these stages. Data were collected through focus group interviews with leaders, teachers, and guardians of tradition, aiming to identify cultural, aesthetic, and mathematical meanings associated with the ritual house. The results indicate that the construction integrates cosmological principles, material resistance, and geometric organization, forming a sacred space of cultural convergence. It is concluded that the Iyaõkwa Hakolone represents a microcosm of the Enawenê-Nawê worldview, highlighting the union between traditional knowledge, social identity, and spirituality.

articles.title: The process of disciplinarization of Descriptive Geometry in Brazil in the 19th and 20th centuries
articles.titleOriginal: The process of disciplinarization of Descriptive Geometry in Brazil in the 19th and 20th centuries
authors: Almeida, Ana Mary Fonseca Barreto de
articles.abstract: The process of disciplinarization of Descriptive Geometry in Brazil is directly related to the creation of the Royal Military Academy of Rio de Janeiro in the early 19th century. Greatly inspired by the École Polytechnique de Paris and created in 1810, the Military Academy introduced Descriptive Geometry as part of its program. This research aimed to analyze the process of disciplinarization of Descriptive Geometry in Brazil in the 19th and 20th centuries, using a qualitative approach based on textual and contextual analysis. The analysis indicated that the process of disciplinarization of Descriptive Geometry in Brazil was characterized, from the outset, as a repetition of methods, created solely as a teaching discipline and not for research.

articles.title: Unit of measurement fathom: ethnomathematics, teaching and learning
articles.titleOriginal: Unit of measurement fathom: ethnomathematics, teaching and learning
articles.abstract: Historically created measurement systems have been preserved by sociocultural groups that continue to use ancestral measures, such as the hectare, the tarefa (units of area measurement), and the fathom (a unit of length measurement), in their daily activities. The objective of the research was to reflect on units of measurement that are cultural heritages as possibilities for teaching and learning mathematical concepts. The theoretical framework draws on authors in ethnomathematics and ancestral measurement; the methodological approach adopted was qualitative ethnographic research. The results show that cultural dynamics can be a strategy for teaching and learning in the ways of mathematizing the environment. It is concluded that this knowledge and these practices in the classroom are one of the ways to challenge the status quo established in an imposed curriculum.

articles.title: Ethnomathematics, displacements, and borders: a study with Haitians in São Paulo
articles.titleOriginal: Ethnomathematics, displacements, and borders: a study with Haitians in São Paulo
articles.abstract: This article presents the results of doctoral research on intercultural education, grounded in Ubiratan D’Ambrosio’s Ethnomathematics Program in dialogue with Paulo Freire. The research aimed to analyze the connections between education and politics in the context of Haitian immigrants’ schooling. To this end, the methodology of being in borders was developed, based on processes of otherness, listening, and dialogue. The research took place in two stages: participant observation at a Youth and Adult Education Center (CIEJA) in São Paulo, Brazil, and interviews with the principal, three teachers, and two Haitian students. The results highlight the relationships established within the school community and point to three boundaries that shape immigrants’ trajectories: racism, professional training, and language.

articles.title: The Boi Pintadinho Festival and School Mathematics Education: a dialogue between colors and knowledge
articles.titleOriginal: The Boi Pintadinho Festival and School Mathematics Education: a dialogue between colors and knowledge
authors: Lorenzoni, Claudia Alessandra Costa de Araujo
articles.abstract: Originating from professional master's research, this paper focuses on the cultural practices of Boi Pintadinho in Muqui, Brazil, and its connection with school mathematics education. The investigation adopts an ethnomathematical perspective, based on D'Ambrosio and Bishop, conceiving mathematics as a human and cultural construction. The text reports on a pilot experiment with a qualitative and ethnographic approach, carried out through participant observation in 2024, recording forms, rhythms, and choreographies. The analysis followed Bishop's activities: counting, measuring, locating, projecting, playing, and explaining. The findings reveal practices intertwined with these processes, integrating cultural knowledge and school mathematical thinking. It is concluded that the ethnomathematical approach offers paths to diversified education and contextualized learning.

articles.title: Between points and knowledges: tensions between school knowledge and traditional knowledge in quilombola handicrafts:
articles.titleOriginal: Between points and knowledges: tensions between school knowledge and traditional knowledge in quilombola handicrafts:
authors: Fantinato, Maria Cecilia de Castello Branco
articles.abstract: This study sought to discuss and identify how quilombola practices and forms of knowledge articulate mathematical knowledge, highlighting the tensions between hegemonic school knowledge and traditional knowledge involved in grass handling. Grounded in discourse analysis, the study examines 36 events involving women and adolescent craftswomen from the Raiz quilombo, located in the municipality of Presidente Kubitschek, in the Espinhaço Mountain Range, Minas Gerais, Brazil. The research involved three participants (women, men, and adolescents) and employed Oral History as a methodological approach, in addition to the observation of everyday activities related to handicrafts. The findings reveal the need to value these local forms of knowledge which, although often marginalized within formal education, hold significant cultural and pedagogical meaning.

articles.title: When Ethnomathematics meets Gert Biesta: possible dialogues and productive tensions
articles.titleOriginal: When Ethnomathematics meets Gert Biesta: possible dialogues and productive tensions
articles.abstract: The research aimed to discuss the dialogue between theoretical contributions from the field of Ethnomathematics and some produced by the educator Gert Biesta, especially those expressed in his work The (Re)discovery of Teaching. With regard to Ethnomathematics, the perspective adopted is that of Gelsa Knijnik, intersecting ideas from Ludwig Wittgenstein's mature work and a set of Foucauldian notions. The results point to the productivity of the dialogues, since the similarities are expressed in three important pillars when considering teaching and learning processes: criticism of learning measurement processes, problematization of scientific advances, and the role of teachers in teaching processes.

articles.title: Ethnomathematics and Architecture: the historic buildings of UFRRJ as a resource for teaching Mathematics
articles.titleOriginal: Ethnomathematics and Architecture: the historic buildings of UFRRJ as a resource for teaching Mathematics
authors: Silva, Débora de Oliveira Couto da
articles.abstract: This study investigated the presence of Ethnomathematics in the buildings of the Federal Rural University of Rio de Janeiro, seeking to understand how architectural elements reveal mathematical practices in cultural and historical contexts. The objective was to analyze how the observation and interpretation of buildings can support pedagogical practices that make mathematics teaching more sensitive to cultural diversity. The research combines a literature review, relating Ethnomathematics, Architecture, and the history of the institution, with visual and structural analysis, considering geometric aspects and constructive solutions. The results indicate that architecture transcends its functional and ornamental character, incorporating mathematical manifestations with cultural value, highlighting its potential as a teaching resource, bringing it closer to students' daily lives.

articles.title: Between files and pedagogical practices: the legacy of Ubiratan D’Ambrosio on the Assessment-Report
articles.titleOriginal: Between files and pedagogical practices: the legacy of Ubiratan D’Ambrosio on the Assessment-Report
articles.abstract: A dialogue is established based on the results of two studies on the Assessment-Report, a model conceived by Ubiratan D’Ambrosio. The first study consists of a postdoctoral research in the Postgraduate Program in Science and Mathematics Education at the Federal University of Uberlândia, and the other in a training workshop involving documents from the Ubiratan D’Ambrosio Personal Archive (APUA). In addition to the aim is sharing investigative and training activities with documents from the aforementioned archive, to contribute to reflections on emancipatory assessment practices in Mathematics Education. In the documentary research at APUA and in the analysis of graduate students' narratives, the Assessment-Report reveals itself as an emancipatory practice that interfaces with the dimensions of the Ethnomathematics Program, respecting the cultural roots of the student and promoting their critical autonomy.

Tanto en el movimiento investigativo documental en el APUA como en el análisis de narrativas de posgraduandos, el Informe-Evaluación se revela como una práctica emancipadora que presenta interfaces con las dimensiones del Programa de Etnomatemática, respetando las raíces culturales del estudiante y promoviendo su autonomía crítica.

A dialogue is established based on the results of two studies on the Assessment-Report, a model conceived by Ubiratan D’Ambrosio. The first study consists of a postdoctoral research in the Postgraduate Program in Science and Mathematics Education at the Federal University of Uberlândia, and the other in a training workshop involving documents from the Ubiratan D’Ambrosio Personal Archive (APUA). In addition to the aim is sharing investigative and training activities with documents from the aforementioned archive, to contribute to reflections on emancipatory assessment practices in Mathematics Education. In the documentary research at APUA and in the analysis of graduate students' narratives, the Assessment-Report reveals itself as an emancipatory practice that interfaces with the dimensions of the Ethnomathematics Program, respecting the cultural roots of the student and promoting their critical autonomy.

articles.title: Geometry descriptors with low assertiveness in the 2015 to 2023 editions of the Minas Gerais (Brazil) external assessment
articles.titleOriginal: Geometry descriptors with low assertiveness in the 2015 to 2023 editions of the Minas Gerais (Brazil) external assessment
articles.abstract: The study aimed to problematize descriptors related to Numbers and Geometry, assessed jointly in the 2015 to 2023 editions of the Proeb. The assessment is positioned as a dimension of the curriculum, focusing on the assertiveness results of the 5th grade of Elementary School, 9th grade of Middle School and the 3rd grade of High School in Minas Gerais, Brazil. Data collection took place via access to spreadsheets with student results from the Minas Gerais Educational Assessment Portal. We considered the average assertiveness results per descriptor with the lowest assertiveness results. Analysis of common descriptors indicates an expected progression in complexity, and that skills considered complex in the 5th grade become structuring in the 9th grade and essential in the 3rd grade. It also indicates that the transition between cycles has not guaranteed the deepening of these skills, generating a cumulative effect of gaps.

articles.titleOriginal: A teaching sequence for the development of statistical literacy in the 1st grade Elementary School
articles.abstract: With this study, an analysis was conducted on the teaching of Statistics in the 1st grade of Elementary School, considering its contribution to scientific thinking. Of a qualitative nature and with a theoretical-propositional character, the study is supported by a recent bibliographic review on statistical literacy in Elementary School and by references from the field. It presents a teaching sequence, which is analyzed based on the theoretical framework, articulating the cognitive and attitudinal components of statistical literacy and the use of concrete materials. Its main objective was to analyze the potentialities and limitations of the teaching sequence, offering contributions that provide support for future research and for teaching practice in statistics education.

articles.title: Mathematics is not neutral: teachers’ conceptions of antiracist education in quilombola communities
articles.titleOriginal: Mathematics is not neutral: teachers’ conceptions of antiracist education in quilombola communities
articles.abstract: This qualitative study aimed to identify the conceptions of teachers who teach Mathematics in schools located in quilombola communities in the municipality of Senhor do Bonfim, Brazil, regarding educational policies addressing ethnic-racial relations. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire, enabling an analysis of teachers' understandings of the current legislation and its implications for Mathematics teaching. The findings indicate that, despite gaps in initial teacher education concerning anti-racist education, teachers recognize the relevance of these policies and identify possibilities for connecting Mathematics teaching with the appreciation of Black culture. The study also reveals teachers' insecurity in addressing racial issues, as well as the positive impact of these practices on students' critical thinking, self-esteem, and sense of belonging.

articles.title: Methodological approach to division: a reflection in light of Angolan Elementary School Mathematics textbooks and the experiences of three teachers
articles.titleOriginal: Methodological approach to division: a reflection in light of Angolan Elementary School Mathematics textbooks and the experiences of three teachers
articles.abstract: This study examined how the division operation is presented in elementary Mathematics textbooks in Angola and how it is taught by teachers. Methodologically, it involved analyzing content and tasks from textbooks for grades 1 to 6, as well as interviews with three teachers. The findings indicate that both textbooks and teaching practices emphasize low-demand tasks focused on mastering the division algorithm. This approach limits conceptual understanding, reducing division to the execution of calculations and procedural rules. The study also identified the absence of tasks that explore the meanings of ratio and combination. It concludes that division is approached in a restricted manner, which hinders the development of meaningful learning and students’ progression to more advanced levels of mathematical understanding.

articles.title: The development of Computational Thinking in mathematical proofs
articles.titleOriginal: The development of Computational Thinking in mathematical proofs
articles.abstract: This paper presents research that aimed to show the possibilities for developing Computational Thinking (CT) in various types of Mathematical Proofs (MP). Using a qualitative research approach, a set of MP was selected, identifying in each of them the practices and processes associated with CT that can be mobilized in each proof. The research conclusions highlight that the articulation between CT and MP favors the understanding of formal notions such as generalization, logical rigor, and argumentative validity, which are fundamental in the teaching and learning processes of Mathematics. This articulation also contributes to the development of systematic, abstract forms of reasoning that can be transferred to different mathematical contexts.

articles.title: Written Text Production in the education of teachers who teach Mathematics: a state of knowledge
articles.titleOriginal: Written Text Production in the education of teachers who teach Mathematics: a state of knowledge
articles.abstract: This article presents a state of knowledge study on written textual production in the education of teachers who teach Mathematics. The aim of this study was to analyze how written textual production has been conceptualized, mobilized, and problematized in Brazilian theses and dissertations. The study is characterized as qualitative, bibliographic in design, taking as its corpus academic works defended between 2006 and 2024 and retrieved from publicly accessible digital databases. The analysis is grounded in sociointeractionist perspectives of language and in the conception of Mathematics as a form of discourse. The results indicate that written textual production assumes different educative statuses — ranging from a didactic resource to a practice of professional development and reflective/narrative writing of teaching —, yet remains weakly institutionalized, revealing the absence of its consolidation as a structuring dimension of Mathematics teacher education.

El estudio tuvo como objetivo analizar cómo la producción textual escrita ha sido conceptualizada, movilizada y problematizada en tesis y disertaciones brasileñas. articles.titleOriginal: The Theory of Mathematics in the Context of Sciences and its theoretical-methodological potential when articulated with other frameworks

El presente estudio analiza las potencialidades teórico-metodológicas derivadas de la articulación de la Teoría de la Matemática en el Contexto de las Ciencias con otros referentes de la Educación Matemática, con énfasis en la enseñanza y el aprendizaje en cursos de Ingeniería. De carácter cualitativo y naturaleza bibliográfica, la investigación se fundamenta en el análisis de estudios desarrollados por los autores, en los que la TMCC se articula con la Teoría Antropológica de lo Didáctico, la Teoría de la Modificabilidad Cognitiva Estructural, la Teoría de los Campos Conceptuales y la Teoría de los Registros de Representación Semiótica. Los resultados evidencian que dichas articulaciones amplían el poder analítico y propositivo de las investigaciones, posibilitando la construcción de una estructura teórico-metodológica más robusta y el desarrollo de prácticas didácticas más consistentes en contextos extramatemáticos.

articles.title: The Geometry and the Mathematical Knowledge Specific to Teaching in Mathematics Teacher Education Programs in Paraíba
articles.titleOriginal: The Geometry and the Mathematical Knowledge Specific to Teaching in Mathematics Teacher Education Programs in Paraíba
articles.abstract: The education of Mathematics teachers reveals tensions between academic knowledge and the demands of Basic Education, especially in the teaching of Geometry. This study aimed to understand how Geometry is addressed in Mathematics teacher education programs at public institutions in Paraíba, Brazil, based on the analysis of Pedagogical Course Projects, with emphasis on course syllabi. This is a qualitative, documentary, exploratory-descriptive study. The results indicate the predominance of Academic Mathematics, with limited articulation with teaching and with Mathematical Knowledge Specific to Teaching. Gaps in initial teacher education are evident, particularly regarding the integration of content, pedagogical practice, and school demands, pointing to the need for curricula that foster the development of professional teaching knowledge.

La formación de profesores de Matemáticas evidencia tensiones entre los conocimientos académicos y las demandas de la Educación Básica, especialmente en la enseñanza de la Geometría. El estudio tuvo como objetivo comprender el enfoque de la Geometría en los cursos de formación docente en Matemáticas de instituciones públicas de Paraíba, Brasil, a partir del análisis de los Proyectos Pedagógicos de Curso, con énfasis en los programas de las asignaturas. Se trata de un estudio cualitativo, documental, de carácter exploratorio-descriptivo. Los resultados indican la predominancia de la Matemática Académica, con una limitada articulación con la enseñanza y con el Conocimiento Matemático Propio de la Docencia. Se evidencian vacíos en la formación inicial, especialmente en la integración entre contenidos, práctica pedagógica y demandas escolares, lo que señala la necesidad de currículos que favorezcan el desarrollo del conocimiento profesional docente.

articles.title: Professional development: action research on in-service teacher education for those who teach Mathematics
articles.titleOriginal: Professional development: action research on in-service teacher education for those who teach Mathematics
articles.abstract: The study sought to identify and understand interactive processes and constitutive elements of the professional development of teachers who teach Mathematics, emerging from collaborative in-service teacher education. Grounded in Vygotsky’s socio-interactionist perspective, in the criteria for effective professional development, and in learning communities, the study was conducted as qualitative action research with five teachers from a public school. Data were produced through field diaries, audio recordings, and teachers’ written productions and organized into dialogical interactive episodes. The results indicate a shift from individual to collaborative planning, the development of tasks with pedagogical intentionality, and the adoption of an investigative stance toward students’ reasoning. It is concluded that the school and peer interaction constitute important conditions for reflective practices and teachers’ professional development.

La investigación buscó identificar y comprender procesos interactivos y elementos constitutivos del desarrollo profesional de profesores que enseñan Matemáticas, emergentes de una formación en servicio colaborativa. Fundamentado en la perspectiva sociointeraccionista de Vygotsky, en los criterios de efectividad del desarrollo profesional y en las comunidades de aprendizaje, el estudio se constituyó como una investigación-acción cualitativa con cinco profesores de una escuela pública. Los datos se produjeron mediante diarios de campo, grabaciones y producciones docentes, y se organizaron en episodios interactivos dialógicos. Los resultados evidencian el paso de la planificación individual a la colaborativa, la elaboración de tareas con intencionalidad pedagógica y la adopción de una postura investigativa sobre el razonamiento de los estudiantes. Se concluye que la escuela y la interacción entre pares constituyen condiciones importantes para prácticas reflexivas y el desarrollo profesional docente.
